Brad Abrahams made a film following men who claim intimate contact with aliens. He joins Danny Jones to discuss the most startling of those claims. They are summed up in the episode's blunt title. His subjects describe abductions and hybrid programs, and Abrahams presents their testimony as a documentarian who lived alongside them.

Jones treats the material with the show's usual open curiosity, neither endorsing nor mocking the witnesses. The claims have no physical verification, and the episode offers none. What it records is stranger and more human: men who believe these things happened to them, explaining what that belief costs and gives. Listeners get the abduction phenomenon from inside the believers' lives, which is where Abrahams's camera spent its time, and where the phenomenon's power plainly lives.
podcast-dannyjones-ZIEGOmwJJxk:
Jeffrey Long joins Danny Jones to present what the episode title calls the best proof yet for life after death. Long is a doctor who built the world's largest study of near-death events. His files hold thousands of reports from people who nearly died.

Long shares patterns that show up across the reports, such as light, peace, and meetings with the dead. He argues the shared details point to a mind that can run apart from the brain. Jones asks how Long answers the doctors who doubt him. Listeners get the strongest case from the man who holds the largest file of such reports.

Rogan's MMA Show returns with number 182, again titled Protect Ya Neck. The side series gathers Rogan with fighters and fight minds. No single guest headlines this session.

The crew reviews recent bouts and argues over styles and calls. Stories from gyms and cages fill the gaps between fights. Rogan's own years calling fights shape the talk. The episode is built for loyal fight fans: loose, loud, and full of the small detail that only people who train and watch closely ever notice or debate. Regulars know the rhythm and settle in fast.
